scope: Legacy JSON preview rejects an idle dismissed callback and never pops a newer route after preview completion.
Trash restore/delete use the original current route, serialize writes, and accept each confirmation at most once.
Canceled stale trash confirm/export callbacks do no work; real failed storage keeps the original snapshot and allows retry.
WebDAV preserves initial local load; dismissed save/backup/disconnect callbacks do no credential or network work.
WebDAV waits for the independent probe cleanup, then checks the original route before upload, readback, or enabling configuration.
limits: Tests use synthetic in-memory repositories/credential stores and a synthetic WebDAV client; no external account or user files are used.
The legacy child-result navigation test exercises the caller continuation; genuine successful restore remains covered by the existing legacy restore suite.
The stale backup test traps any credential read locally before real transport construction; it demonstrates zero operation entry after dismissal.
Already-authorized durable writes may finish after navigation changes. This change does not promise rollback after store.save has begun.
Real TLS/WebDAV server interoperability and broad native/end-to-end acceptance are separate validation suites.
